title: A fixed 30-plant sample gave no clear change in ozone and moisture slopes in four eastern US forest samples in 1994-2010
abstract: We tested whether plant sampling effort changes an ozone and soil moisture association with visible leaf injury. We used a verified published panel and 4,834 site-years in two eastern US regions and two periods from 1994 to 2010. We computed the exact chance to find injury in a random subset of 30 examined plants. This reduced mean detection by 4.6 to 10.2 percentage points. On matched records, the four changes in annual ozone and moisture product slopes were +0.015, +0.019, +0.050 and +0.020 probability units per 10 ppm-h ozone per soil moisture SD. All four two-way cluster 95 percent intervals included zero. Ten-plant and 60-plant checks and an effort control also gave no clear slope change. Thus a fixed effort changed detection levels, but the data did not show a clear change in these slopes. This does not prove equal slopes or remove species selection, missed injury or exposure error. The calculation is conditional on recorded plants, not a new field survey or a causal estimate. The package gives original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and a verified-source retrieval command.

display.caption: Ozone and moisture slopes on the same records before and after a fixed 30-plant calculation (A), and their paired changes (B). Bars show two-way state and year cluster 95 percent intervals. All four paired intervals include zero.

citations.reason: Verified source panel and original raw-source processing; this is a same-data observation-effort audit, not independent data validation.
Annual product decomposition and region-period scope inform the model. We write new code and test a paired change of outcome.
